page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.e family. It is configured with 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is shared. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance has no local storage and does not include any GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results position this instance primarily in the average to lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with PassMark CPU and memory scores, fall within the average category. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 570.8 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 80.28 GB/sec. However, single-threaded performance is a bottleneck, as shown by poor results in Geekbench single-core, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores are weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this instance represents a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or high-speed local disk access. It is suitable for static web serving and Redis operations, both of which achieved average benchmark performance. The instance is also appropriate for basic software compilation and lightweight database operations, but is less suited for CPU-intensive single-threaded tasks or memory-heavy applications due to its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance within the ecs.e family, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 shared vCPUs (4 physical cores with hyper-threading), 16.0 GB of RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates average performance for multi-core CPU tasks, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, though single-threaded performance in compression and text processing is poor. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-effective solution for non-critical, moderately threaded workloads. It is best suited for static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and basic software compilation tasks that do not demand dedicated CPU resources.
